verdict_rationale: Model-C score progression from P90 to P99 identifies increasingly severe macro trend deterioration. However, score severity actively worsens adverse prevailing excursion (+2.04 ATR at P99 vs +1.78 ATR at P90; 99.1% extending >= +1.00 ATR and 100.0% extending >= +0.75 ATR) and fails to localize entry: immediate fade expectancy deteriorates from -0.016 ATR at P90 to -0.032 ATR at P99. While temporal delay to a winning zone drops from 110s to 15s, taking an immediate fade entry at P99 is guaranteed to hit a -0.75 ATR stop before reaching the reversal. Therefore, P90 was NOT simply 'too early' on a monotonic timing curve; Model C inherently reflects macro deterioration velocity rather than local turning-point geometry, and moving deeper into the score tail does not make the signal economically actionable without an independent causal timing mechanism.
recommendation_for_next_experiment: Cease attempting to extract execution entry timing directly from Model-C score levels or tail quantiles. Treat Model C strictly as an upstream macro regime-deterioration gate (ARMED state), and test an explicit causal microstructure / order-flow / price-action trigger (e.g. 1-second delta absorption, failed continuation break, or local micro-regime change) during the post-P90 window to time the actual +1.00/-0.75 ATR entry.
